Walnut Creek School Board · Election Day Nov 3, 2026
# Common sense for Walnut Creek's schools.
Public schools are where a community comes together — across classrooms, neighborhoods, and generations. When we support them well, every family and all of Walnut Creek grow stronger.
Donate to the CampaignGet a Yard SignVolunteer
Meet the neighbors and community leaders supporting Geetha
Our version of picture perfect
Official endorsement
## Officially endorsed by the Walnut Creek Teachers Association
I come from a family of educators! I was raised to see teachers as the people who hold a community together. I'm honored to have the support of the educators who show up for our kids every day. I'm also proud to have earned the backing of local political organizations whose endorsements are among the hardest to win. They looked closely at my record and my plans for our schools and chose to stand behind this campaign. Visit my Endorsements page to see everyone who's standing with me.
## Endorsed by leaders and neighbors across Walnut Creek
- Sarah Butler, President, Contra Costa Co. Board of Education
- ·Craig DeVinney, Walnut Creek City Council
- ·Nithin Iyengar, Former WCSD Board Member
- ·Mary Britton, Retired Teacher & WCSD Grandparent
- ·Walnut Creek families & educators
Read every endorsement
Questions, inquiries, or want to learn more? Contact ggforschoolboard@gmail.com
Priorities
## Four questions guiding every decision.
### Academic Foundations, Done Right
Strong reading, math, and science. With enough teacher support to make it work.
Explore this priority
### Critical Thinking First, Then AI
Kids learn to think for themselves first. Then they learn to use tools like AI. No hype, no panic.
Explore this priority
### Health & Well-Being
Mental health, movement, and real support. Kids can't learn well without them.
Explore this priority
### Accountable, Evidence-Based Governance
Real evidence. Clear trade-offs. Decisions the board follows through on.
Explore this priority
See my full priorities
Parcel tax information for seniors & homeowners
## Understanding the parcel tax before you vote.
You deserve more than a request for your trust. You deserve the information to make that decision for yourself.
Supporting strong schools and asking hard questions are not opposites. In fact, I believe they belong together.
When our community is asked to make another financial commitment, voters should be able to understand why it is needed, what has changed, how the money would be used, and how we will know whether it is making a difference.
That is why I went through the data myself and put it here in plain English.
Look at the numbers. Ask the questions. Decide what you think.
As a former journalist, and someone who takes pride in community empowerment, I believe this is essential.
One question to start with
How much would Measure W cost a Walnut Creek home over eight years?

Who I am
## A mom who started asking questions, and kept going.
I'm Geetha Ganti, a mom of two kids in Walnut Creek schools. I have a background in journalism — I started my career as a health journalist at CNN and later worked as a local television reporter, where my job was to ask hard questions and explain the answers in plain English. Since then, my background in public health and engineering has taken me into healthcare leadership — finding real savings and using new technology responsibly, without losing sight of the people it's supposed to help. That's the job I want to do on the school board: ask good questions, follow the evidence, and explain the answers so every family can understand them.
“I spend most of my time trying to understand the real problem before deciding what to do next.” — Geetha Ganti
